title: From Abstract Reduction to an Explicit Closed Form
content: The parent entry proves that every power of a matrix reduces modulo the characteristic polynomial — Aᵏ = (Xᵏ mod χ_A)(A) — but leaves the reduced polynomial implicit. This file makes that reduction completely explicit in the smallest nontrivial dimension, n = 2, where χ_A has degree two and the recursion closes into a single second-order linear recurrence. The headline is Mⁿ⁺¹ = u(n+1)·M − (det M · u n)·I, with u the Lucas sequence of X²−(tr M)X+(det M). The result is fully general: any 2×2 matrix over any commutative (nontrivial) ring, with no eigenvalue or diagonalisability hypothesis.
mathContext: With $t=\operatorname{tr}M$, $d=\det M$, Cayley–Hamilton gives $M^2=tM-dI$. Writing $M^{n+1}=a_nM+b_nI$ and multiplying by $M$ yields $a_{n+1}=ta_n+b_n,\; b_{n+1}=-da_n$, whence $a_n=U_{n+1}$, $b_n=-dU_n$ for the Lucas sequence $U_0=0,\,U_1=1,\,U_{k+2}=tU_{k+1}-dU_k$.
relatedConcepts: Lucas sequences of the first kind

title: The Lucas Sequence of the Characteristic Polynomial
content: lucasU t d is the Lucas sequence of the first kind attached to the monic quadratic X²−tX+d: u₀=0, u₁=1, u(k+2)=t·u(k+1)−d·u(k). It is defined by structural recursion on ℕ with the two base cases 0 and 1, so the defining recurrence lucasU_add_two holds by rfl. Specialising the parameters recovers familiar families: (t,d)=(1,−1) gives the Fibonacci numbers, (2,−1) the Pell numbers, and (t,1) Chebyshev-like sequences. These scalar coefficients are exactly what the matrix closed form needs.
mathContext: $U_n(t,d)$ with $U_0=0,U_1=1,U_{k+2}=tU_{k+1}-dU_k$. When the discriminant $t^2-4d$ is a square with roots $\alpha,\beta$, $U_n=(\alpha^n-\beta^n)/(\alpha-\beta)$ (Binet form).

title: Cayley-Hamilton in the 2×2 Case
content: sq_eq_trace_smul_sub_det_smul derives the explicit identity M² = (tr M)·M − (det M)·I. It starts from Mathlib's Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly (χ_M(M)=0) and rewrites χ_M via Matrix.charpoly_fin_two (= X² − C(tr M)·X + C(det M)). The simp set evaluates aeval on the polynomial, turning C-coefficients into scalar multiples through Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one and collapsing (r•1)·M to r•M via smul_mul_assoc/one_mul. The residual equation M² − (tr M)•M + (det M)•1 = 0 is rearranged into the stated form by eq_of_sub_eq_zero together with a single abel step, which handles the additive-group bookkeeping among the three matrix atoms.
mathContext: For $M\in M_2(R)$, $\chi_M(X)=X^2-(\operatorname{tr}M)X+\det M$ and Cayley–Hamilton gives $M^2-(\operatorname{tr}M)M+(\det M)I=0$.

title: The Closed Form by One-Step Induction
content: pow_succ_eq_lucasU_smul proves Mⁿ⁺¹ = u(n+1)·M − (det M · u n)·I by ordinary induction on n. The crucial observation is that the successor step needs the inductive hypothesis at only one previous index, not two: rewriting Mⁿ⁺² = M·Mⁿ⁺¹ (pow_succ') and substituting the closed form produces a term M·(c•M) = c•M², which the 2×2 Cayley-Hamilton identity immediately reduces — so no two-step induction is needed. After pushing M through the scalar multiplications (mul_smul_comm) and unfolding the Lucas recurrence (lucasU_add_two), match_scalars splits the matrix equation into two scalar identities in the free R-module on {M, I}, each closed by ring. The reindexed pow_eq_lucasU_smul restates the result as Mⁿ = u(n)·M − (det M · u(n−1))·I for n > 0.

title: Showcase: the Fibonacci Matrix
content: For fibMatrix = !![1,1;1,0] the trace is 1 and the determinant is −1, so the Lucas recursion u(k+2)=u(k+1)+u(k) is exactly the Fibonacci recurrence — the closed form becomes Mⁿ⁺¹ = F(n+1)·M + F(n)·I, the matrix encoding of the Fibonacci numbers. fibMatrix_sq instantiates the closed form at n=1 and checks M² = !![2,1;1,1], i.e. !![F₃,F₂;F₂,F₁]. The numeric witness is closed by kernel `decide` (not native_decide), so the entry remains axiom-free.
prerequisites: trace and determinant of a concrete 2×2 matrix
